name: Cisplatin + 5-FU with concurrent radiotherapy (definitive / neoadjuvant, esophageal SCC)
cyclesNote: Cisplatin plus infusional 5-FU given concurrently with definitive-dose radiotherapy (about 50 to 50.4 Gy) for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; commonly two cycles during radiation with further cycles after, per physician judgement.

institution.provenance: StewardMD ONCOTREE draft protocol authored from standard guidelines (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Cisplatin is highly emetogenic; give a 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone and an NK1 antagonist before cisplatin per emetic-risk guidance.

premedications.name: Hydration
premedications.notes: Pre- and post-cisplatin IV saline hydration with magnesium and potassium repletion to protect renal function.

supportiveCare: Concurrent radiotherapy to a definitive dose (about 50 to 50.4 Gy); coordinate chemotherapy timing with the radiation plan.
Nutrition support and management of radiation esophagitis / dysphagia throughout treatment.
Aggressive antiemesis and renal-protective hydration around cisplatin.
monitoring: renal function and serum magnesium before each cisplatin dose
CBC before each cycle and during concurrent radiation
audiometry / neuropathy assessment for cumulative cisplatin toxicity

doseModificationRules.text: Reduce or hold cisplatin, or substitute carboplatin, for declining renal function; physician decides.

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.notes: Cisplatin 75 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of a 28-day cycle, concurrent with definitive-dose radiotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Requires renal-protective hydration and magnesium repletion. Dose and schedule are a standard-of-care description (StewardMD wording); physician decides and the dose engine computes the patient dose.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU)
drugs.notes: 5-FU 1000 mg/m2 per day as a continuous IV infusion on days 1 to 4 (about 4000 mg/m2 per cycle), every 28 days, concurrent with radiotherapy. Standard esophageal chemoradiation backbone; monitor for mucositis, diarrhea, and hand-foot syndrome. StewardMD wording; physician decides.
